mathematical_findings: The open-ball covers are indexed by the dependent sum of all patch indices and patch points; neither index type is required to be countable.
Global precise_refinement produces a locally finite open cover for each reciprocal-natural radius. Passing to its range preserves local finiteness while removing duplicate set values.

For a fixed point x, point finiteness makes the subtype of patches containing x finite. Positive local ball radii give natural thresholds; an upper bound of their finite range yields one radius suitable in every such patch.

A refining member containing x is contained in a metric ball from a patch that necessarily contains x. The triangle inequality bounds the distance of every member point from x by twice the selected radius, establishing the basis condition.

The reusable point-finite cover theorem needs paracompactness but no separation assumption. The final metrization theorem obtains T3Space from explicit T2Space plus paracompactness before invoking full Nagata-Smirnov.

The unrestricted main equivalence is exactly MetrizableSpace X iff T2Space X and ParacompactSpace X and LocallyMetrizable X. The specialized equivalence fixes Hausdorff local metrizability and characterizes paracompactness.

LocallyMetrizable asks for open metrizable subspace neighborhoods. This is equivalent to the source's metrizable-neighborhood condition by restricting to an open neighborhood inside a given metrizable neighborhood.
There are no second-countability, separability, countable-cover, or countable-layer hypotheses.

Empty X and empty cover index types are handled without Nonempty or Inhabited assumptions. Where a point exists, the cover witness supplies a containing patch; finite-range boundedness itself also handles an empty finite subtype.
The compatibleMetric constructor uses the newly proved MetrizableSpace instance, and compatibleMetric_topology checks definitional compatibility with the supplied topology.
